build_purpose: Minecraft replica of Hunt Midwest SubTropolis, the world's largest underground business complex in Kansas City, Missouri. Carved into the south wall of a deep ravine/gorge in the same mountain range as Cheyenne Mountain Complex.

scale.horizontal_compression: ~1:100 floor area (200x200 Minecraft blocks representing ~55 million sq ft mined void)
scale.pillar_to_pillar_spacing_blocks: 30-40 at iconic intersections (relaxed from real 65-block spacing for buildability)

footprint.description: Main underground grid: 200x200 blocks (X: -100 to +100, Z: 0 to -200). Centered on the build's coordinate space.

main_avenue_description: Total length from south portal surface to east portal surface: ~140 blocks entrance ramp + ~200 blocks main avenue through grid + ~10 blocks exit ramp. Runs E-W along the long axis of the ravine wall.

world_origin.description: Main entrance portal at surface level, on the south face of the SubTropolis hill. Y=70 is just above sea level (sea level = Y=64).

compass_orientation.description: The mine extends into negative Z (north) from the south-face portal. The ravine is further north. Cheyenne Mountain is on the north wall of the ravine. The Kansas City plain is to the south (positive Z).

main_entrance_portal_surface.description: Main entrance portal at world origin, south face of SubTropolis hill. 12x5 portal frame, branded marquee sign, 'SPEED LIMIT 15' sign, security gate, guard booth.

main_entrance_ramp_grid_level.description: Where the entrance ramp meets the main grid. South end of the main avenue.

main_avenue_start.description: South end of the Hushpuckney main avenue, just inside the grid.

main_avenue_midpoint.description: Central intersection of the main grid. Hunt Hall (round room, 30x30). Hushpuckney Ave runs N-S through this point; Bethany Falls Blvd runs E-W.

main_avenue_end.description: North end of the main avenue, at the edge of the grid.

second_exit_portal_grid_level.description: Where the exit ramp begins, at the east edge of the main intersection.

second_exit_portal_surface.description: Second exit portal on the east face of the SubTropolis hill, perpendicular to the main entrance. 12x5 portal frame, smaller surface lot, exit-only security booth.

hunt_midwest_visitor_center.description: Small modern office building on the surface plateau. Houses the leasing office, Lamar Hunt interpretive plaque, mounted Chiefs arrowhead, 'SubTropolis - Est. 1964' plaque, FTZ sign, ENERGY STAR 100 certificate.

parking_lot_stub.description: 4-6 row surface parking lot south of the visitor center. Compressed from the real 1,600+ spaces.

public_shaft_surface_exit.description: Surface lobby for the public shaft, on top of the SubTropolis hill. Players exit here to access the city in the broader valley.

worlds_of_fun_silhouette.description: Distant single tower or roller-coaster silhouette representing the Worlds of Fun amusement park that sits above the real SubTropolis. Faded reference only.

tenant_zones.name: USPS Stamp Distribution Center
tenant_zones.description: Multi-bay loading dock with dock doors, USPS livery, semi-trailer, dock leveler, small commemorative-stamp display. Visible from the main avenue.

tenant_zones.name: USPS Stamp Fulfillment Center
tenant_zones.description: Package conveyor layout, fulfillment operations. Adjacent to the Stamp Distribution Center.

tenant_zones.name: EPA Region 7 Training & Logistics Center
tenant_zones.description: Emergency-response signage, smaller fit-out. The 'mole people' aspect is here: the EPA chose SubTropolis for its climate stability.

tenant_zones.name: NARA Federal Records Center
tenant_zones.description: Climate-controlled archive with rows of archive boxes on industrial shelving, dim amber lighting, climate-control signage, NARA eagle logo on the door. The 2012 lease of 102,000 sq ft (with options to 372,000) was the largest single federal move into the complex.

tenant_zones.name: SubTropolis Technology Center (STC)
tenant_zones.description: Sealed data center chamber with server racks (redstone lamp props), red/green status lights, blue LED floor lighting, biometric hand-reader prop at the door, 'SubTropolis Technology Center' sign, visible 'DARK FIBER - 1102 GRAND' conduit run. ENERGY STAR 100 rated. Sleek, modern, visually distinct from surrounding 1960s industrial aesthetic.

tenant_zones.name: W.W. Grainger distribution
tenant_zones.description: Long chamber with rows of pallet racking, pick-and-pack station, shipping manifests on whiteboards. The 2026 expansion makes it the largest known underground distribution center in the world. Replaces the historical Ford 25-acre vehicle-storage lease.

tenant_zones.name: Hallmark / Russell Stover general industrial
tenant_zones.description: Packaging-line tenant fit-out. Hallmark Cards, Russell Stover, and Pillsbury are all early-tenants. General industrial archetype: pallet racking, conveyor, packaging.

tenant_zones.name: Underground Vaults & Storage (UV&S)
tenant_zones.description: Small secured vault with three rows of metal shelving, a few unlabeled film cans, and a single small label reading 'GONE WITH THE WIND - INTERPOSITIVE' or 'WIZARD OF OZ - MASTER'. UV&S is the 'distributor of last resort' for major American film studios. No movie posters, no green-ray imagery.

tenant_zones.name: Hunt Hall (central plaza)
tenant_zones.description: 30x30 round room at the main intersection. Lamar Hunt interpretive plaque on the wall, mounted Chiefs arrowhead. No Chiefs helmet, no football imagery. The Hunt family ownership is the content; the Chiefs is one bullet point, not the theme.

tenant_zones.name: Leasing office (visitor center interior)
tenant_zones.description: Interior fit-out at the south end of the main avenue. Plaque reads '14,000,000 SQ FT DEVELOPED'. FTZ sign. ENERGY STAR 100 framed certificate. Tenant list. Hunt Midwest corporate signage.

tenant_zones.name: Visitor center interpretive wall
tenant_zones.description: Wall text: 150 ft below surface (with 'up to 160 ft' noted as maximum), 68 F year-round (65-70 F range noted), 1964 founding year, 8.2 mi of paved road, 18,000-24,000 psi compressive strength, ENERGY STAR 100 since 2012, 50-70% energy savings. Geology exhibit on Bethany Falls limestone.

tenant_zones.name: Employee cafeteria (faded)
tenant_zones.description: Small faded room with tables, a coffee station, a vending machine prop. An 'atmospheric easter egg' per the Operations Manager - the things that aren't in any press release but that workers remember.

tenant_zones.name: Ghost mine (unfinished chamber)
tenant_zones.description: Dark, raw rock, no paint, no lights, no paving. Blocked by a barricade with 'DANGER - ACTIVE MINING - HUNT MIDWEST MINING, INC.' sign. Parked mine cart or equipment prop. Deliberately unreachable. Conveys that most of the 55 M sq ft is unfinished.

side_spurs.name: Side spur 1 (west)
side_spurs.description: Branches west off the main avenue. Leads to the ghost mine chamber. Single-lane, vehicle-traversable.

side_spurs.name: Side spur 2 (east)
side_spurs.description: Branches east off the main avenue. Leads to the STC support zone and additional tenant space. Single-lane, vehicle-traversable.

service_tunnel_to_cheyenne.from_description: SubTropolis service sub-basement, below the main grid. Accessed by a downward corridor from (-80, 20, -180) to (-80, 10, -180).
service_tunnel_to_cheyenne.to_description: Cheyenne Mountain maintenance sub-basement (designed by the Cheyenne team).
service_tunnel_to_cheyenne.path_description: Horizontal, single-lane, running under the ravine floor at Y=4-9 (sub-basement level). Connects a Cheyenne Mountain maintenance sub-basement to the SubTropolis service sub-basement. Tagged [X] as a project fiction - this tunnel does not exist in the real SubTropolis.

subtropolis_features.sub_basement: Service sub-basement at (-80, 10, -180): small vehicle turnaround, maintenance bay, signage 'SERVICE TUNNEL - COMBINED COMPLEX MAINTENANCE - AUTHORIZED VEHICLES ONLY'.
subtropolis_features.downward_corridor: 10-block vertical corridor from (-80, 20, -180) to (-80, 10, -180) with a security gate.
subtropolis_features.vehicle_support: Minecart-compatible for the player. Visually designed for a small service vehicle (John Deere Gator, Cushman, mine-spec buggy).
subtropolis_features.security: Security gate between the tunnel and the SubTropolis grid. SubTropolis is private property; the service tunnel connection is a real security concern.

public_shaft_to_city.from_description: Public Access Lobby at the SubTropolis grid edge.
public_shaft_to_city.to_description: Surface lobby on the SubTropolis hilltop, where players step out onto the plateau to access the city in the broader valley.
public_shaft_to_city.path_description: Vertical shaft running from the SubTropolis grid at Y=20 up through the ravine wall to a surface exit at Y=90. Tagged [X] as a project fiction - the real SubTropolis has no public shaft; it is accessed by a private drive.

subtropolis_features.lobby: Public Access Lobby at (60, 20, -180): security guard booth, turnstile, 'PUBLIC TRANSIT - COMBINED COMPLEX' sign, visible vertical shaft (long vertical line that the player can see going up).
subtropolis_features.vertical_shaft: 5x5 blocks, 70 blocks vertical, from Y=20 to Y=90. Player-climbable with ladders or a Minecraft elevator.
subtropolis_features.surface_exit: Surface lobby at (60, 90, -180) on the hilltop plateau. Players step out onto the surface and can navigate to the city in the broader valley (which connects to the Houston tunnel system in the combined-complex project).
subtropolis_features.security: Staffed entry - a security guard booth and a turnstile. A facility that is normally access-controlled cannot have a public entrance without that.

street_signs.name: Hushpuckney Ave
street_signs.description: Geology-themed street name from the real SubTropolis (named after a local rock type, per the 2010 Atlantic and 2026 Axios reporting).

street_signs.name: Bethany Falls Blvd
street_signs.description: Invented companion to Hushpuckney, named after the Bethany Falls Limestone formation. Candidates for the architect to choose from: Iola, Winterset, Galesburg, Mound City, Drum, Chanute. Tagged [X] - not a documented street name but plausible per the deliberation's approval of 1-2 invented companions.

marquee_at_entrance.text: WORLD'S LARGEST UNDERGROUND BUSINESS COMPLEX (R) - HUNT MIDWEST SUBTROPOLIS

foreign_trade_zone_sign.text: DESIGNATED U.S. FOREIGN-TRADE ZONE - LARGEST UNDER ONE ROOF

depth_interpretive.text: 150 FT BELOW SURFACE (up to 160 ft maximum)

exterior_limestone.strata_technique: Alternating 1-2 block horizontal layers to convey sedimentary layering.

combined_complex_notes.cheyenne_position: North wall of the ravine, ~400-600 blocks away across the ravine floor.
combined_complex_notes.houston_position: In the city in the broader valley, beyond the SubTropolis hill. Connected via the public shaft (player travels up the shaft to the SubTropolis plateau, then south to the city).
combined_complex_notes.geology_difference: SubTropolis hill is Bethany Falls limestone (sedimentary, cream/beige, layered). Cheyenne Mountain is granite (igneous, gray, crystalline). Both in the same mountain range, but very different rocks.
combined_complex_notes.service_tunnel_path: Horizontal, 6x5 block cross-section, running under the ravine at Y=4-9.
combined_complex_notes.public_shaft_path: Vertical, 5x5 block cross-section, running from the SubTropolis grid at Y=20 up to the SubTropolis hilltop at Y=90.
combined_complex_notes.public_accessibility_difference: SubTropolis is the 'open to the public, mixed use' leg of the trilogy. Cheyenne is military / secure / single-use. Houston is pedestrian / downtown. The public shaft makes SubTropolis the most publicly accessible of the three.

deliberation_topic_references.topic_1_scale: 200x200 footprint, 1:1 vertical, 8x8 pillars, 5-block ceiling, ~350-block main avenue, two ~100-block side spurs. Compression ~1:100 floor, 1:1 vertical. No 'big cavern' rooms.
deliberation_topic_references.topic_2_must_haves: Tier 1: horizontal portal, pillared corridor grid, second portal. Tier 2: geology-themed street names, painted pillar numbers, 15 mph speed limit, multi-tenant variety (6+), ghost mine chamber. Tier 3: STC, constant-climate feel, surface plateau with Hunt Midwest visitor center.
deliberation_topic_references.topic_3_source_conflicts: 55M at marquee / 14M in leasing office / 16 ft ceiling / 150 ft depth / 55+ tenants / 1964 / 68 F / 8.2 mi road. Hierarchy of numbers: marketing at threshold, technical fact in back office.
deliberation_topic_references.topic_4_creative_license: Mandatory [D]/[I]/[X] legend. Four fit-out archetypes: records archive, package logistics, data center, general industrial. 'Operationally plausible' inventions.
deliberation_topic_references.topic_5_easter_eggs: Prominent: USPS (with dock-door scene), NARA, STC (with biometric + dark fiber), EPA, 'World's Largest Underground Business Complex' (R). Subtle: UV&S film archive (one labeled can), Hunt Hall (one plaque, one mounted arrowhead), FTZ sign, ENERGY STAR 100 certificate, employee cafeteria. Out: Indiana Jones, Batcave, Bond villain, torches, fake idols, mob spawners, movie posters, helmet imagery.
deliberation_topic_references.topic_6_combined_complex: Service tunnel: 6x5, sub-basement, security gate, vehicle turnaround. Public shaft: 5x5, Public Access Lobby with guard booth and turnstile. Both tagged [X] as project fictions. Service tunnel runs under ravine to Cheyenne. Public shaft goes from grid up to hilltop.

open_questions_for_architectural_designe: Geology-themed street name companions: Iola, Bethany Falls, Winterset, Galesburg, Mound City, Drum, Chanute are candidates (per Topic 5 deliberation).
Surface plateau size: 100x100 around visitor center, or 200x200 matching mine footprint?
Hunt Hall exact location, size (30x30 suggested), and rotation.
Data center detail depth: rack depth, status light animation, biometric hand-reader prop.
NARA high-bay shelving: nearly-ceiling-height archive shelving (Operations Manager argued for this).
Inter-site coordination with Cheyenne Mountain and Houston tunnel-system teams: cross-section compatibility.
Rail spur detail: parked boxcar on a short track (faded reference).
Visitor center interpretive wall content: text layout, image panels.
Employee cafeteria design: tables, coffee station, vending machine prop.
Worlds of Fun silhouette: single tower/coaster in the distance, at what distance?
Service tunnel sub-basement access: location and integration with ghost mine chamber.
Public shaft lobby integration: on main avenue or side spur, security gate configuration.
